sam (eng-ml): quick sync — ran KV-only quant bake on rwdx-13B: FP8-kv vs INT8-kv vs baseline fp16. results surprised me, posting short summary + commands.

sam (eng-ml): high level: FP8-KV gives ~2.1x KV memory savings vs fp16, INT8-KV ~2.7x. but cold-start p95 jumps for INT8 on H100 in our harness. FP8 has slightly higher peak throughput when KV is hot.

sam (eng-ml): numbers (single A100-80GB perf run, seq_len=1024, batch=1, kv_len=1024):
```
baseline fp16: mem_kv=11.2GB, p50=24ms, p95=42ms
fp8-kv: mem_kv=5.3GB, p50=22ms, p95=45ms
int8-kv: mem_kv=4.1GB, p50=26ms, p95=68ms (cold tails)
```

anika (research): can you paste the exact quant flags + kernel toggles? also which kernel library?

sam (eng-ml): used quantize_kv.py + runtime flags:
```
# quant build step
python tools/quantize_kv.py --model rwdx-13B --mode fp8 --per-channel true --calib-samples 40k --out /tmp/q_fp8
# runtime (cpp serving)
--kv-quant-mode fp8 --enable-kv-cache --kernel=cpu-gemm/kernelex
```

sam (eng-ml): for int8: --mode int8 --calib-samples 80k and runtime --kv-quant-mode int8 --int8-deq-bias-correction true

ben_pratt: hmm the int8 cold tail sounds like dequant overhead + fallback to slow kernel. did you observe any kernel fallback logs?

sam (eng-ml): yes logs show: `using int8_kv_dequant_v1` then occasionally `falling back to int8_dequant_scalar` under contention. that fallback path adds ~30–50ms.

anika (research): did you run AWQ/GPTQ style per-channel vs per-tensor for kv? int8 per-channel helps stability but increases calib time.

sam (eng-ml): tried 3 variants: int8-per-tensor, int8-per-channel, int8-awq (symmetric + grouped). per-channel reduced EM/QA delta but didn't remove tail. AWQ had best quality (tiny regresses) but still had fallback latency on H100 in our stress tests.

eva_research: what about quality metrics? any eval sets (QA exact match / instruction evals)?

sam (eng-ml): quick eval (1000 prompt QA set):
```
baseline fp16: EM=84.6
fp8-kv: EM=83.9 (-0.7)
int8-kv (per-channel): EM=83.2 (-1.4)
int8-awq: EM=83.7 (-0.9)
```
note: these are small-sample; distribution matters (long-context prompts show slightly larger delta for int8).

ben_pratt: small EM drops okay for non-critical paths, but for SLAs we need <=1% EM regression. also need p95 stability.

anika (research): curious: where are the memory wins coming from? is KV dense tensor quant only or including past kv buffers + optimizer state?

sam (eng-ml): only KV cache tensors (keys + values); model weights unchanged. so savings directly reduce per-request memory footprint which improves capacity per-GPU.

sam (eng-ml): another interesting datapoint: warm-path throughput (streaming, KV hot) on A100: fp16 baseline 180 tok/s, fp8-kv 200 tok/s, int8-kv 190 tok/s. so fp8 gave best throughput when kernel stays hot.

eva_research: any HW variance between A100 and H100? we should avoid rolling int8 if H100 shows inconsistent fallback behavior.

sam (eng-ml): yes H100 had more aggressive kernel switching in our runtime (probably because different warp shapes). H100 int8 p95 was 90ms in worst-case runs.

anika (research): actions? suggestions:
- add a kernel health check: if dequant fallback frequency > 1% in 1h, mark int8-kv unhealthy for that region.
- promote fp8-kv as default KV quant for now (smaller quality delta + stable kernels).
- run 5k sample eval focusing on long-context docs to quantify tail quality.

sam (eng-ml): agree. I'll open canary rollout: fp8-kv by default with int8-kv as opt-in reserve for high-capacity customers.

eva_research: also add automated eval: EM and MRR + token-level perplexity on long-context set; threshold for auto-rollback: EM drop >1.0 or pPPL increase >3%.

quant-ci-bot: CI:kv-quant-bake #1769 finished — artifacts: https://ci.redwood/kv-bake/1769 (perf traces + kernel logs) :white_check_mark:

ben_pratt: thanks, can you attach the trace where fallback happened (we need stack + kernel name) and we'll file a runtime bug for scalar fallback path?

sam (eng-ml): added trace link in the CI artifacts. filing runtime ticket now @eng-runtime.

anika (research): small note for docs: add a short guidance paragraph under "KV quant" about cold-starts and kernel compatibility across HW. i'll draft.

sam (eng-ml): thanks — going to put fp8-kv bake into canary for us-east-1 dedicated cluster tomorrow 09:00 UTC. ping here once canary is live. :rocket:

eva_research: sweet, please include telemetry counters: dequant_fallback_count, kv_cache_hits, kernel_switch_count, per-request mem bytes.

sam (eng-ml): will do. end.
